items.title: 66095_Benny Carter oral history interview
items.q: I had Miles Davis in the band in '46.

ctx.x: I think I know your answer to this, but I'm gonna ask it anyway -- did you feel that these guys were playing something new that you wanted to have part of your band, or were you again, just picking up good musicians, playing good music or whatever it was?

Well, I felt that, certainly they had something new, different, fresh, young. And something I liked -- and I did want to have them with the band, and as a matter of fact, I had Miles Davis in the band in '46.
Yeah. A little bit later -- maybe in one of these pickup bands that you would put together for a few dates, rather than keep them indefinitely, you also had Wardell Gray.

items.title: Carter Benny — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Miles Davis was in the band in ’46, something, and he was with it for just a short time, maybe a matter of weeks.

ctx.x: You just mentioned that a lot of people were getting drafted. Was that the only reason these people came in, or did you want to inject a different kind of sound or you were attracted to some of these younger musicians?

No, but, I mean, some of those I replaced because they went into the service. But, no, I don’t know. Just, you know, J. J. Johnson joined me in Indianapolis [Indiana] and came to California with me. Now, when Max Roach came into the band, I don’t remember. Miles Davis was in the band in ’46, something, and he was with it for just a short time, maybe a matter of weeks.
You picked him up in St. Louis [Missouri], is that correct?
